Nutrients adversely affecting bone health
Vitamin A
Vitamin A refers to a family of essential, fat-soluble compounds called retinoids. Retinol is the principal dietary form of vitamin A.
The main natural sources of vitamin A are provided by animal foods such as liver, meat, milk products, eggs, and fatty ﬁsh. In addi-
tion, some foods are fortiﬁed with vitamin A. Cod liver oil (which is commonly used in a number of population groups, particularly
postmenopausal women/elderly) also contains high levels of vitamin A. There are approximately 600 or so carotenoids, with
approximately 10% of these having provitamin A activity.
